definitions.explanation: Literary first-person pronoun referring to oneself, mainly preserved in proverbs, classical writing, and a small set of formal expressions about self-reflection.

examples.japanese: {己|おのれ}に{打|う}ち{勝|か}つことが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It is important to overcome oneself.

examples.japanese: {敵|てき}を{知|し}り{己|おのれ}を{知|し}れば、{百戦|ひゃくせん}{危|あや}うからず。
examples.english: Know your enemy and know yourself, and you need not fear a hundred battles.

notes:
Literary and old-fashioned word for 'self'. Modern Japanese uses {自分|じぶん} in nearly all everyday contexts; {己|おのれ} survives in proverbs, classical-style writing, and a few set phrases about self-mastery.

FIXED EXPRESSIONS:
- {己|おのれ}を{知|し}る: to know oneself
- {己|おのれ}に{勝|か}つ / {打|う}ち{勝|か}つ: to overcome oneself
- {己|おのれ}を{律|りっ}する: to discipline oneself
- {己|おのれ}を{捨|す}てる: to set aside the self

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {自分|じぶん}: oneself — the everyday word; use this in normal speech
- {我|われ}: I; self — literary, formal speeches and writing
- {自我|じが}: ego; the self — psychological/philosophical term
